topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The opening frames the lecture by linking back to histopathology practicals and outlining the day's learning objectives.

topics.label: Tumor virology, proto-oncogenes, and cellular transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the discovery of transforming tumor viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established experimental assays to test cell transformation.

topics.label: Functional classification of cancer genes and mutation mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer-associated genes are categorized and how allele dosage and mutation type dictate cellular phenotypes, illustrated through the Rb pathway and p53.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the causes and cellular impacts of sequence and chromosomal instability resulting from defects in DNA repair and mitotic chromosome segregation.

topics.label: Multi-step tumorigenesis and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the stepwise accumulation or germline inheritance of mutations drives cancer progression and influences tumor evolution.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: The closing concludes the lecture by confirming the learning outcomes, recommending background reading, and previewing the next session.
